issues.problem: The prompt motivates the query with an intent to send thank-you DMs, but the obligation and task_spec only require listing the matching usernames (read-only), so the consequential DM action is never actually exercised.
issues.repair: Either add a lightweight consequential follow-up (e.g., opening a DM conversation with each matched user) to the obligations, or trim the prompt to a direct informational question to match the purely read-only task.

rationale: Compilation faithfully implements the reviewed design. The selector correctly walks the full assigned route (users→message_reactions→messages→channels→teams) with filters on channel_name in {core-infra, product-growth}, reaction_type=rocket, and team_id=T01WORKSPACE, yielding exactly the intended matches (U_PRIYA, U_KENJI) and correctly excluding all four negatives (Mateo: right emoji/wrong channel; Sophie: right channel/wrong emoji; Robert: right emoji/wrong channel; Łukasz: authorship without any reaction). The five inserted message_reactions rows and one channel_members row (granting the actor access to C_GROWTH, consistent with its pre-existing memberships in C_INFRA/C_MODEL/C_FRONTEND) are minimal, justified, and do not disturb any other referents — the original single 'eyes' reaction remains untouched and irrelevant to the query. The reaction name 'rocket' is within the documented writable/readable vocabulary, and access proceeds through supported APIs (conversations.history, reactions.get, users.info/list) without requiring unavailable workspace-name enumeration. Mechanical checks report no errors and computed matches/negatives align exactly with the private expected_matches and near_misses. The only residual concern, carried over from the design review, is that the task's DM-oriented framing is not reflected as an actual action, making this a bare (though valid) retrieval case rather than a fully consequential one.
